sections.heading: Gift ideas for birthdays, couples, and special milestones

blocks.text: For a birthday, request a solo hero debut poster with a custom hero name and a Quirk concept in the order notes. Energetic poses, mid-laugh photos, and expressive hand gestures work especially well for a confident character introduction. For couples, consider a rival-heroes composition or a partner rescue scene, using coordinated costume colours without making both characters look identical.

A graduation portrait can celebrate someone entering a new stage of life: add a bold background, a determined stance, and a short phrase such as “Plus Ultra” in your personal notes if appropriate. Sports fans may enjoy a Sports Festival-inspired action pose, while roommates or friends can become a small hero agency squad. The concept can be light-hearted, dramatic, or age-appropriate for a younger fan.

sections.heading: How to turn a photo into a My Hero Academia-inspired cartoon portrait

blocks.text: Ordering a custom anime portrait from photo is straightforward. Choose the My Hero Academia-inspired style, upload a clear reference image, and describe the character you want the artist to create. You do not need professional photography: a well-lit phone photo is usually enough when the face, hair, and shoulders are visible. Avoid cramped crops if you want a costume with visible arms, gloves, support gear, or Quirk effects.

items: Select a photo with a clear face and recognisable expression.
Describe the desired pose, mood, costume colours, and background energy.
Add the imagined Quirk, such as fire trails, gravity waves, energy gloves, or a completely new ability.
Mention any group arrangement, including who should stand in the centre and how people should be positioned.
Check the preview within 72 hours and request any changes needed.

blocks.text: The artist uses your likeness as the foundation. Eye shape, smile, hair colour, and distinguishing marks remain important, while the hero costume and effects are built around you. This means the portrait looks like the recipient rather than a generic anime character. Anime Cabinet provides unlimited free revisions, so you can request adjustments to the expression, colours, pose, costume details, or background before approving the artwork.

sections.heading: What details should you provide for a custom portrait commission?

blocks.text: The more useful context you provide, the easier it is for the artist to translate your idea into a cohesive original hero design. Along with the reference photo, explain who the gift is for and what feeling the artwork should convey. A few focused notes are better than a long, conflicting list of instructions.

items: The recipient’s name, nickname, or optional hero name.
Preferred costume colours, clothing details, accessories, and level of coverage.
A Quirk idea, visual effect, or personality trait to express through the pose.
Whether the artwork should feel funny, heroic, intense, cute, or suitable for a child.
The preferred background, such as a training arena, city skyline, colour burst, or clean poster layout.
For group portraits, each person’s position, height order, and relationship to the others.

blocks.text: You can also mention what should not appear. For example, ask for no weapons, a softer costume tone, fewer effects, or a simple background suitable for a bedroom. These details help artists create a polished fan-art inspired portrait without copying a specific copyrighted character.
